headline: Akashvani Bhavan Security Guard Becomes National Celebrity After Declining To Ask For Autographs During High-Profile Trespassing Incident
body:
Ramesh Kumar, a junior security guard at Akashvani Bhavan, has reportedly become the most sought-after man in the capital after he famously stood his ground during a recent high-profile protest, refusing to pause his morning newspaper crossword to ask the participating leaders for selfies or autographs. While political tension flared around the main entrance, Kumar was spotted calmly checking staff ID cards and noting down the exact count of sugar sachets remaining in the canteen, completely unfazed by the presence of prominent opposition figures.

“They were pushing through the gate, and honestly, all I could think about was whether I had locked the cupboard containing the station’s spare microphone cables,” said Kumar, who has now been offered three book deals and a reality show contract for his ability to maintain professional apathy in the face of national news. “I did ask one of them if they had a visitor’s pass, but they were too busy shouting slogans about institutional integrity to check their pockets. I suppose they didn't have one, so I just went back to my Sudoku.”

Management at the broadcasting house has lauded Kumar as the 'Employee of the Month,' citing his decision to prioritize canteen inventory over political spectacle as a masterclass in bureaucratic focus. “Most people would have been starstruck or terrified, but Ramesh simply maintained that the guest book had to be signed in black ink only,” said the station’s facility manager. “When the protestors demanded to be heard, he merely pointed to the sign saying 'No Talking in the Lobby During Tea Break,' effectively silencing a complex political agitation with a single laminated piece of paper.”
caption: A security guard at Akashvani Bhavan has achieved legendary status for prioritizing his crossword puzzle during a major political protest. Discipline, after all, knows no party lines. (satire) #AkashvaniBhavan #IndianPolitics #WorkLifeBalance #Satire
igHook: Would you have stopped to ask for a selfie, or just kept doing your job like this absolute legend?
imagePrompt: A wide, slightly blurry shot of a nondescript, functional office building entrance in India, featuring a glass door and a metal barricade, with a generic security guard uniform hanging on a nearby chair in the foreground.

sourceHeadline.title: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi booked over forcible entry into Akashvani Bhavan during INDIA bloc protest

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 wins by grounding a chaotic political situation in a perfectly mundane, relatable detail: the guard's crossword puzzle. Its warm, bureaucratic tone feels much more like an Onion-style satire than the other entries, which rely too heavily on the 'mistaken identity' trope that repeats across the batch.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictionalized security guard character to satirize bureaucratic apathy and is clearly framed as a humorous piece. It does not target specific public figures in a harmful way, avoids sensitive communal or caste themes, and the image prompt is generic.
